scope: Ideal early-time contact mechanism, not biological temperature/sensation prediction

primary_model_source.citation: Strotos et al. (2011), International Journal of Thermal Sciences 50(5), 698-711, section 3 equations 1-5

derivation: Each side has a semi-infinite error-function solution. Matching Fourier fluxes gives Tc=(eA TA+eB TB)/(eA+eB), with e=sqrt(k rho cp). Signed A-to-B flux is eA eB/(eA+eB)*(TA-TB)/sqrt(pi t); integration gives Q/A=2 eA eB/(eA+eB)*(TA-TB)*sqrt(t/pi).
assumptions: Planar perfect thermal contact; one-dimensional conduction
Early times before finite thickness or external boundaries matter
No contact resistance, moisture, roughness, blood flow or sensory adaptation
guardrails: No default material numbers; test inputs are explicitly synthetic solids
Use kelvin in the model; Celsius differences are equivalent but labels must remain explicit
Do not show the ideal instantaneous contact change or t=0 flux singularity as measured human response
Thermal conductivity alone does not determine transient contact response
Heat flows from warmer to cooler; reverse arrows when the object is warmer
All arrows and temperature fields are schematic unless an independently measured experiment is supplied
No source figures or text copied into output; citation does not license their assets
